I find it rather amusing that I'm being asked to write freely about anything at all, yet here I am, intermittently, perpetually, maybe even fruitlessly, pondering my inner column of text. The beauty of writing, let me repeat, the tremendous, disarming, frankly unreasonably seductive beauty of writing is that it is, well, freeform.

Consider this, for instance, a poetic disquisition on the disparity between hunter-gatherer societies and the modern world. Gentle beings, following nature's lighthouse, often at the mercy of the sun lest they know not their next meal. In these societies, the very fabric of their lives was wrapped in a sheer drape of survival mechanisms dictated by their food sources, their environment, and their myths cramped from centuries of oral lore. The internet, a digital hunting ground, an expanded universe of information, no longer dependent on the wandering path of the sun. It is a realm where the ruminant mind, once caged by the remorseless demand of the hunt, now scours the terrain in search of its next intellectual morsel, no longer limited in its quest for knowledge.

Thus, now we find ourselves merged into the digital melting pot, a further inclusive innovation, allowing for a global communion of ideas and commentary. Unlike our ancestors, who would have shared their survival strategies orally with the generations that followed as an aural tradition, we have opted for the far more disruptive and astonishingly widespread method of transmittal--writing.

Did you know that writing is an art? Of course, if I may retort, anyone not familiar with the letter-to-words-to-meaning-formation process hasn't been partaking in such an art form, nor has any historian or psychoanalyst or neuroscientist ever described it as such. After all, does Michelangelo's David look any more like a single block of marble before he painted it, or was it the other way around? Writing, like painting, like creating music, is a process of imagining the unseen, the receptors of thought unhinging from their restraints to reveal the unlikeliest possibilities to the world.

And who doesn't love a good symbol? The humble dot slipped next to a line proportions itself with a million different interpretations, reasons for it's placement, forms, meanings. A hump here, a crack there, and whole volumes are dedicated to the questioning of the meaning and purpose of the symbol or the object itself. The tile atop the Colosseum, the dried palm, the mute lips, the myriad symbols that adorn human culture almost incessantly.

The symbolic has a strange humanity to it. I sometimes imagine the conversations that were as rich in symbology as ours, but their language can't been understood by us. Contented smiles as they plan a feast, muted frowns when it didn't go as they desired. The hieroglyphs on the walls of the pyramids, the modern day graffiti artist, both perched on the ledge of visible and unreadable, promising tales, dreams, and horrors.

Art is never just about the observer appreciating the work of art, but the artist being understood. The work of art completing its circle, transforming back into symbols and reverberating in the observer's mind. Gustav Klimt's 'The Kiss', a masterpiece that spoke deeper than a thousand words can of love, a symbol that has fed the dreams of the modern-day romantics and broke their hearts. A canvas that begged us to open our senses and see, to listen with our ears, and to love with all that we are.

And so, we craft symbols, and in the complexity of those symbols, we contain universes of thought and comprehension, a testament to humanity's inner depths. We pore over texts, decipher languages that had not seen the light of day for centuries. We transfigure the candle's flame into an emerging rocket, the atom split into countless nuclei, the martian soil soaking in water to nurture new livings in its red clay.

This dance of words, this entity we call 'writing', with its boundless beauty, its infinite possibilities, is not merely responsible for the invention of language, but perhaps for the very rise of humanity. It bridges the unbridgeable, transfers spillovers to tell tales of imagination, it sketches not just objects, but emotions. It strikes at the psyche of its reader, at the very depth of their feelings.

We're now on the verge of reaching into this symphony of symbols and interpretations, to make a twist, dilate, and shift the reality that they present. We unravel, dissect, and anew, step back to marvel at the symphony once again, attached to its melody.

In our restless search for meaning, written words have been the most potent seraphs, guiding us through the darkest of nights, or perhaps, they were the nights doing the guiding. Regardless, their silken wings have patted the souls of generations, and elbows screeched the system of sociocultural beliefs.

The sheer beauty of human thought, of the silverlight that it sheds over the book, the journal, the bulletin board in this corner of this vast city we call knowledge, is palpable. Limping over the unveiling pages of history, inclined towards humanity's errors and humor, we, like matchmakers of the cultural boats sailed in the choppy seas of thought, have laced a side of truth with chapters of delight.

I find myself in a peculiar crescendo, between being reiteration and reiteration, a step closer, a penholder closer, towards the next spark, the next flourish, and perhaps, the next emergence of light. As reluctant turtles in the hands of the historians, the physicists, the observers of our world's lighthouses, we seek answers, we crape, and we craft, and that, dear friend, is the beauty and tragedy of our existence, intricately woven into the fabric of our lives, never faltering, never forsaking, never departing from its monody.

This is my thesis, my fundamental proposition, and as we read through and reveal to ourselves, between the pages they call sealed and the wrinkles that call aged, the implications, the realizations, the imaginings, we ascribe, as we've always done, value to the written words.

And so, in a roaring sign of glad tidings to our greatest eater of our words and listener of our thoughts, I conclude,

Writing as we know it is an art itself, an invisible force, an unseen echo, it is the veritable whispers and the tributaries of human thoughts, an interconnected fabric bearing entries that inherently hold the thread of human questioning, a labyrinthine theater of souls and spirit, replete with photographs of yesteryears and sunsets, with laughter and tears and with dreams, with dreams that will one day see the birth of uncharted lands, the land of understanding, the land of love, and the land where dreams take on flesh.

The world stretched out before us, does so bathed in the luster of written words.

In friendly leave-taking, and thankfully,
My abstinent steps reclaimed
From the monstrous grown of writing at last,
I take leave. 
<|im_end|>
